subject: Biotechnology
title: Patent Law and Biotech
description: A short lesson to help you apply Patent Law and Biotech.

hook.text: Can you patent a gene? In 2013 the Supreme Court said no to natural DNA — but yes to synthetic cDNA.

buildup.text: Myriad Genetics held patents on BRCA1 and BRCA2 — charging $3,000 for a breast cancer risk test no competitor could offer.

discovery.text: The Supreme Court ruled in AMP v. Myriad that isolated natural DNA is not patentable — it is a product of nature.

twist.text: CRISPR patent battles between the Broad Institute and UC Berkeley lasted a decade — billions hung on who invented it first.

climax.text: Patent pools and licensing agreements now share CRISPR access — collaboration replaces litigation for academic users.

punchline.text: Discover or invent? The line between nature and innovation defines biotech patents.

quiz.question: Why did the Supreme Court rule that isolated natural DNA cannot be patented?
options: DNA is too small to be considered an invention
Isolating a naturally occurring DNA sequence does not create anything new — it is a product of nature
The patent had already expired by the time the case was decided
